correctness.rationale: Encoding the b occurrences by sorted preceding-a counts t_i gives S=sum t_i, Q=2H+S=sum t_i^2. For <=2 b the elementary symmetric polynomial roots are forced; for <=2 a the Vandermonde multiplicities are forced. At total length seven only (k,m)=(4,3) or (3,4) can collide: enumeration of the 35 three-element multisets and the one-dimensional nullspace of the 4-column moment matrix yields exactly the claimed pairs. For three b and gaps x=t2-t1, y=t3-t2, 3Q-S^2=2(x^2+xy+y^2). For norm 7^r, the factorization 7=(3+omega)(3+omega^2) in the Euclidean Eisenstein integers gives 6(r+1) signed norm representatives. The closed nonnegative sextant has r+1 points for r odd and r+2 for r even; reflection exchanges nonzero congruence classes 2x+y mod 3, so exactly floor(r/2)+1 admissible points have residue one. The chosen S and k satisfy t1>=0 and t3<=k by 2x+y,x+2y<=2 sqrt(R); each point yields a distinct valid word. A fresh independent direct-subsequence enumeration confirmed precisely two length-seven doubletons and no shorter collision; exact norm-shell enumeration verified the explicit formula for r=1..6.

value.rationale: The four measurements are a natural fixed low-cost nonadaptive observation in word reconstruction, and the sharp shortest collision as well as unbounded ambiguity with only three markers determine precise information-theoretic limits. An exact all-r fiber formula is mathematically more substantial than a small-census experiment, and a future reader can use it when choosing distinguishing query sets. Neither the general integer moment encoding nor Eisenstein unique factorization alone establishes this observation-specific boundary.

final_claim: For binary words, counts of a,b,ab and aab scattered occurrences uniquely determine every word through length 6, have exactly two doubleton fibers at length 7, and are injective for at most two b symbols at every length. With exactly three b symbols, for R=7^r, L=ceil(sqrt(R)), k=2L+1, S=3L+1, H=(S^2+2R-3S)/6, the fiber (k,3,S,H) has exactly floor(r/2)+1 words for all r>=1.
limitations: Finite enumerations cover n<=7 and r<=6 only; the all-r theorem depends on UFD and sector counting.
No formula for arbitrary observation fibers or the global maximum fiber at every length.
